PROJECT STAFF WILL REPAIR AND PROTECT VULNERABLE BOOKS, MAPS, AND OTHER DOCUMENTS AS NEEDED. OPEN-SOURCE DIGITAL REPRESENTATIONS OF IDENTIFIED MAPS AND BOOKS WILL BE LOCATED, AND KGS-OWNED MAPS AND BOOKS WILL BE SCANNED FOR ONLINE DISSEMINATION. 2) THE KGS DYE TRACE DATASET WILL BE MODERNIZED TO CONFORM TO FAIR DATA STANDARDS AND IMPROVE ITS OVERALL USEABILITY. PROJECT STAFF WILL SCAN AND INDEX ALL PRIMARY PAPER RESOURCES, LINK THESE SCANNED FILES TO THE PREVIOUSLY UPDATED GEOSPATIAL DATA, AND ARCHIVE THE PAPER RESOURCES. 3) NEARLY 100 CUBIC FEET OF PAPER LOGS REPRESENTING APPROXIMATELY 8,000 OIL AND GAS WELLS DRILLED IN SOUTH-CENTRAL KENTUCKY WILL BE IDENTIFIED AND SCANNED AT 300 DPI FOR ONLINE DISSEMINATION. 4) KGS STAFF WILL WORK TO UPDATE KGS METADATA IN THE NEW USGS RESCICOLL REGISTRY OF SCIENTIFIC COLLECTIONS. 5) KGS STAFF WILL (I) GEOREFERENCE AND VECTOR DIGITIZE CRITICAL MINERAL PROSPECT AREA AND DRILL HOLE FIELD MAPS PERTINENT TO THE ILLINOISKENTUCKY FLUORSPAR DISTRICT (II) DEVELOP A DETAILED PLAN FOR VISUAL ANALYTICS, AND INFORMATION EXTRACTION OF GEOLOGICAL CONTENT OF DIGITAL MINING DOCUMENTS, AND (III) COLLECT AND SUBMIT 200 SAMPLES FROM OUR LEGACY SAMPLE COLLECTION FOR GEOCHEMICAL ANALYSIS.DELIVERABLES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES  THE MAJOR DELIVERABLES ARE 1) NEWLY DISCOVERED COLLECTION ITEMS AND RESEARCH DATA WILL BE WELL-ORGANIZED AND MADE AVAILABLE FOR ONLINE AND IN-PERSON WORK  2) AN UPDATED DIGITAL DATASET THAT INCLUDES THE PRIMARY REFERENCES THAT ARE CURRENTLY UNAVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC  3) NEW MATERIAL WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE ONLINE THROUGH EXISTING KGS ONLINE SEARCH AND MAP SERVICES  4) INCREASED DISCOVERABILITY OF MANY KGS DATA COLLECTIONS AND SAMPLE CATALOGS BEYOND THE KGS WEBSITE  AND 5) (I) A NEW MINE MAP COVERING THE ILLINOISKENTUCKY FLUORSPAR DISTRICT WILL BE CREATED AND PUBLISHED, (II) DEVELOP A DETAILED PLAN FOR VISUAL ANALYTICS, AND INFORMATION EXTRACTION OF GEOLOGICAL CONTENT OF DIGITAL MINING DOCUMENTS, AND (III) GEOCHEMICAL ANALYSIS DATA TO HELP ASSESS THE CRITICAL MINERAL POTENTIAL OF AREAS OF KENTUCKY THAT ARE NOT PART OF ON-GOING INVESTIGATIONS.INTENDED BENEFICIARIES  THESE DELIVERABLES WILL BENEFIT KGS STAFF, UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS, AND SCIENTISTS IN KENTUCKY INTERESTED IN VARIOUS AREAS OF KENTUCKY GEOLOGY AND AVAILABLE GEOLOGIC SAMPLES. SPECIFIC BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO RESEARCHERS INTERESTED IN THE KARST LANDSCAPE OF KENTUCKY, MINERAL EXPLORATION AND HYDROCARBON STUDIES, AND CRITICAL MINERALS IN KENTUCKY.SUBRECIPIENTS - N A
